pages.title: About Me
pages.content: Hi! I am John Vernie C. Dela Cruz, an aspiring software engineer and UI/UX designer. I love building full-stack web apps, designing interfaces in Figma, and fixing laptops while questioning every life choice that led to cable management. My goal this semester is simple: center a div on the first try without invoking ancient CSS dark magic, and survive another round of runtime exceptions.

pages.title: Hobbies
pages.content:
• Building web apps and predictive dashboards that actually compile
• Fixing laptops and desktop components while questioning every life choice that led to cable management
• Playing OPM acoustic mashups with a capo on the first fret
• Watching movies with chicken and mango shake

pages.title: Skills
pages.content:

• Computer hardware diagnostics, assembly, and systems troubleshooting
• Data preprocessing and time-series application logic

pages.title: About Me
pages.content: I am Charella Magalpoc, a student of BSIT 3-1 with an interest in systems engineering and computer graphics. When I turn a model on the screen, I like to think about how the program keeps track of every point. A question as simple as that can take me from a drawing on paper to an afternoon of experimenting with code.

pages.title: Hobbies
pages.content: A model in Blender usually begins with a familiar object. I like to turn it slowly under a light and see which details make its shape recognizable. Away from the screen, I play the electric bass. Learning a difficult passage reminds me of practicing a route in a retro game. In either case, the small corrections matter more than the speed of the first attempt.

pages.title: Skills
pages.content: I approach technical problems by looking for one change I can test. If an object vanishes from a scene, I check its position before rebuilding it. If a program stops responding, I try to reproduce the problem before restarting it. The following skills help me carry out those checks and keep a record of the changes that worked.

pages.title: Projects
pages.content: The desk in our group portfolio poses a small but interesting problem. A visitor clicks a flat screen and expects to pick up an object in a three-dimensional scene. Raycasting connects those two actions. My other project interests include a model of the solar system and a small physics engine. Both begin with the same question: how should an object move?

pages.title: Fun Facts
pages.content: I can spend more time choosing the colors of my terminal than using the command that prompted me to open it. I also enjoy explaining how rotations work. A request for the time probably does not call for a lesson on quaternions, though a clock face does make a surprisingly convenient illustration. I try to give the time first.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content: I hope to contribute to open-source graphics libraries and develop simulations that help people investigate scientific questions. If one of the projects in this book reminds you of a problem worth exploring, you may leave a message in the desk guestbook. I would especially like to hear what you would try to represent and which details you would keep in a first model.

tagline: Quality over quantity. Designing practical tech that helps people.

pages.title: About Me
pages.content:
Hi! I am Nicole Leigh G. De Guzman, a BSIT 3-1 student. I focus on practical design and clean code.

Objective
To be able to contribute and work on practical, yet meaningful projects where I can grow and continuously improve my skills in both design and development, while genuinely helping people.

I build prototypes in Figma and write object-oriented Java programs. I care about making software that is easy to use and works properly.

pages.title: Software and Skills
pages.content:
My coursework and daily tools cover both interface design and programming.

Design and Prototyping
Affinity Designer, Figma, and Canva

Visual Presentation
Clean documentation and clear layouts

Programming
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Basics in Java

I like creating clean interfaces in Figma, then turning those layouts into well-structured code.

pages.title: Interests
pages.content:
Outside of schoolwork, I spend my free time on a few personal hobbies.

Stationery and Pens
I collect quality pens, especially 0.38mm fine-nib pens and smooth notebook paper.

Skincare and Fragrance
I like researching skincare ingredients and trying different scents like green tea, cedarwood, and jasmine.

Notebook Layouts
I enjoy keeping neat notes with clean margins and green accents.

pages.title: Core Values
pages.content:
I always choose quality over quantity, and it genuinely bothers me if I leave something unfinished or slightly off.

Whether I am drawing a layout in Figma or writing a Java class, I take the time to fix uneven margins and check my work before moving on.
